challenge: Release-1 'no migration' is a conflict with ratified scope, not merely a 'tension'. Draft 10 frames it as a tension; draft 20 says CNV-ECO-004 'is supported' without noting that the supported segment needs migration first.
evidence: CNV-EXP-002 has release_scope 'initial-implementation'. The CNV-ECO-003 amendment (2026-11-25) requires the first paying sponsor's contract to include a shadow replay of at least 12 months of that sponsor's own grant and contribution history, which needs extraction from the incumbent. CNV-ECO-004 targets sponsors that already run systems. The proposed R1 scope (17-RELEASE-1-SCOPE.md line 108) defers UNB-XIN-OTH-002 with 'no migration in R1'. The R1 document is proposed, not ratified.
recommended_revision: Record this in 22 as a conflict for the owner, not a tension. Options: (a) make history extraction plus read-only history import plus the CNV-EXP-002 reconciliation report a gate for R1 or R1.x before the first paying sponsor; (b) narrow CNV-EXP-002's release scope through the amendment process; (c) choose a greenfield first sponsor, which contradicts CNV-ECO-004. Draft 20 should state that its INCLUDE_IN_FEE result assumes migration exists.

challenge: Several designs assume the incumbent will cooperate, and public incumbent terms deny that. The affected designs are: daily legacy delta feeds for the shadow run (17 S07/S02; the 10 design); legacy read-only for at least 90 days (17); packages signed by the source vendor and redirection of legacy logins (11); repeated production-volume extracts for at least 3 rehearsals (11).
evidence: NPact §2.4 allows access 'only by accessing such products by direct login'. NPact makes export and migration a paid Professional Service and deletes data 10 business days after hosting ends; its initial term is 3 years with 90-day notice. Foundant returns data 'at the time of termination' through reporting tools, 'as stored', with 'no other obligation to maintain' it. TIFIN terms bar downloading and automated access. Ren iPhi gives 15 days (draft 10, internal). Nothing in DAF obliges an incumbent the way FINRA 11870 obliges a carrying member ('both members must expedite').
recommended_revision: Add a per-source Extraction Plan to drafts 13 and 15. It should record the contract end date, notice deadline, the export rights the sponsor holds as data owner, the export method allowed (direct-login reports, paid PS, database backup) and its cost, and the number of extracts the contract allows. Keep legacy read-only in Unbound's own L0 vault, not on the incumbent's servers. Make shadow-run frequency depend on allowed extract cadence; default to periodic manual exports when automated access is banned. Draft 20 should budget incumbent PS, tail and remaining-term fees.

challenge: The 'Sponsor Switching Guarantee' borrows credibility from CASS and ACATS, but those schemes rest on rule- or scheme-mandated obligations on both sides. DAF has no such obligation, and donor-level transfers between sponsors are discretionary.
evidence: ACATS obliges both firms and allows exceptions only from a closed list (FINRA 11870). CASS is a scheme its participants are bound to. Fidelity Charitable: trustees have 'exclusive legal control', and donors 'have no legally enforceable right' to a recommended grant. Draft 11 §5.1 has no term for a late, incomplete or non-conforming source package. Its only exclusion is 'no slot means no guarantee clock'.
recommended_revision: Keep the terms Unbound controls: rehearsal gates, the quiet period, queued recommendations, the freeze on the Unbound side, redirection from Unbound's own crosswalk, and exit symmetry. Start the clock only when a conforming source package is received, and list source-side delays as explicit exclusions. Drop the claim of CASS/ACATS equivalence, or rename the offer a 'Migration Service Commitment'. Cost the service credits in draft 20. Never offer a guarantee to donors about transfers between sponsors.

challenge: Portability depends on who the legal sponsor is. A bank, RIA or wealth-firm 'program' run on a vendor's sponsor (Ren RCF, NPT, Charityvest, Fidelity-type) does not own the fund assets and may not control the donor records. Moving such a program is fund-by-fund discretionary granting (CNV-ENT-002), not a CNV-EXP-002 platform migration. Drafts 11 and 20 do not split CNV-ECO-004's advisor-distributed segment along this line.
evidence: Foundant §6.1 and NPact §6.2: the customer owns Customer Data when the customer is the sponsor. Foundation Source programs are 'sponsored and administered by Charityvest'. Ren RCF 'will create an investment account with Customer' (ONB-021), and the Ren RAC MSA returns only 'Customer Materials' (internal audit). Fidelity trustees have 'exclusive legal control'. Draft 14 does separate migration_kind; drafts 11 and 20 do not.
recommended_revision: Rejected for self-sponsored books on SaaS: ownership is clear in the published templates. Upheld for distributor-on-vendor-sponsor programs. Add a 'legal sponsor of record' question to T0 in draft 13. Model that sub-segment in draft 20 as a sponsor-to-sponsor transfer, which needs the incumbent sponsor's cooperation and has no full-history import. Exclude it from the Guarantee.

challenge: The onboarding economics leave out material costs on both the buyer and the Unbound side.
evidence: Absent from parameters and model code: incumbent tail and dual-run fees (draft 10 cites JCF paying Ren $417,742); remaining-term or cancellation fees (NPact) and paid export PS; incremental auditor procedures for a new service organisation; legal review (DPA, privacy notice, program terms); donor and advisor communication production; at least 3 rehearsal runs (draft 11); pre-contract assessment at T2-T4 (draft 13); Guarantee service credits; a failed-migration reserve (FFTC paid Give $654.5k before abandoning, an INFERENCE; akoyaGO reports 85% on-time migration tasks); sales and CAC. Check: at 10k accounts revenue is $4.13M against $480k recurring cost (88% margin), so these omissions do not change INCLUDE_IN_FEE at 10k accounts or more. They do change it for 1k-5k sponsors and for buyer TCO.
recommended_revision: Add a buyer switching-TCO table (sponsor staff, incumbent fees, audit, legal, communications) separate from Unbound's P&L. Add Unbound lines for rehearsals, a risk reserve, service credits and CAC. Re-run R14 for small sponsors. Say explicitly that the result at 10k accounts or more is driven by revenue (see ADVB-13).

challenge: Automation moves work onto sponsor finance and IT, and draft 20 undercounts it: 530 sponsor hours (about $37k) at 10k accounts.
evidence: The drafts assign the sponsor at least 10 duties: run the T1 profiler; give A4 confirmation of every mapped column; confirm each restriction class; fix-in-source exceptions; prepare explained differences; CFO and finance dual approval of the reconciliation report; controller approval of gate results on each of at least 3 rehearsals; choose remediation for unsupported behaviours; accept the risk on the verified-payee share; sign the cutover decision. Evidence from draft 10: Hartford spent 4 months on training and clean-up plus 2 months of dual run; TAG says large foundations need at least 0.5 FTE or a consultant; 990 Part VII-B consultant lines run $115k-$724k a year. sponsor_fixed_h (250 h at 1k accounts) is an ASSUMPTION with no source.
recommended_revision: Model sponsor hours duty by duty, using the duty list in drafts 13-17. Show the range against the case evidence. Offer a priced, Unbound-staffed 'sponsor-side analyst' option, keeping segregation of duties for A4 approvals. Measure in the first migration (CNV-ECO-003 evidence obligations). Present the drafts as reducing consultant spend, not removing customer work.

challenge: Draft 20 calls full-history import (CNV-EXP-002) the largest cost driver but models only 7 years of history. Meanwhile some predecessors cannot supply full history at all.
evidence: history_years is 7 in economic_model.py. Many national sponsors are decades old. AEF's pilot pulled 33 months and shows 2 years (ADVB-005), so its successor cannot obtain full history from that platform alone. The CNV-EXP-002 acceptance criterion requires 'no unexplained difference'.
recommended_revision: Set history_years by sponsor age (for example 7, 15 and 25) with a volume ramp, and re-run R5 and R7. Propose a CNV-EXP-002 clarification: 'full history available from any source the sponsor can lawfully obtain; gaps disclosed as HistoryGap (14) with the source's retention evidence'.

challenge: Accounting conventions: the drafts make no epoch design for CNV-FIN-007 grant recognition point. A legacy convention that differs (recognise at payment or at approval) changes grants payable and expense at E, and a change needs the external auditor to accept the policy.
evidence: CNV-FIN-007 requires an effective-dated GrantRecognitionPoint and a period-end cutoff register (approved-uncommunicated, communicated-unpaid, conditional). Its activation gate is the external auditor's acceptance in the first audited year. Only draft 12 (config) mentions it. Drafts 14, 16 and 17 have rules for units, fees and accruals but none for recognition point.
recommended_revision: Standardised migration is not impractical: draft 16's unit and fee design holds. But add a CNV-FIN-007 epoch gate: detect the legacy convention at T0/T1, build the cutoff register at E-1, carry the legacy convention to fiscal year-end unless the auditor concurs earlier, and reconcile grants payable under both conventions.

challenge: AI mapping risk. The nondeterminism concern is answered (AI is excluded from transforms). The residual risk is semantic mis-mapping that keeps totals intact, which round-trip control totals cannot detect.
evidence: Draft 13 makes a mapping usable once round-trip totals pass and the sponsor confirms it. Totals do not change when advisor and successor roles are swapped, restricted and unrestricted are mixed up, grant status is wrong at the same amount, or acknowledgment flags are wrong. Human confirmation of AI proposals moves the work back to the sponsor (ADVB-06). No public evidence was found that auditors accept or reject AI-assisted mapping.
recommended_revision: Add semantic invariants per entity (role cardinality, status-transition legality, restriction class against sampled fund agreements, acknowledgment-to-contribution linkage). Add stratified record-level sampling that the sponsor attests. Add mutation tests that inject total-preserving swaps and must be caught. Record AI provenance for each mapping decision in the auditor pack.

challenge: Draft 16 makes the auditor the primary consumer of the migration evidence. A new entrant will not have a SOC 1 Type II report that covers the first sponsor's audit period, so the sponsor's auditor will likely do more substantive work at the sponsor's cost.
evidence: Practitioner guidance says Type II periods are usually at least 6 months and should overlap the user's audit period. Unbound's requirements already design for SOC 1 Type II (RCD-031). Neither the migration drafts nor draft 20 budget for the gap.
recommended_revision: Plan a SOC 1 Type I at go-live and a Type II window that overlaps the first sponsor's fiscal year. Time the first epoch for that overlap. Add sponsor audit-fee uplift to the buyer TCO.

challenge: Internal inconsistency on lock-in. Draft 20 recommends 36-60-month terms and a termination fee that recovers onboarding cost. Draft 10 ranks those same mechanics as switching barrier #6, and the exit-symmetry pitch in drafts 10 and 11 relies on Unbound not having them.
evidence: ECO-RC-5; draft 20 §4 table; the barrier ranking table in draft 10; the exit-symmetry rows in drafts 10 and 11.
recommended_revision: Publish a declining onboarding-recovery schedule up front, with export never conditioned on payment and no export fee. Or drop the exit-symmetry claim. Do not market 'no lock-in' while contracting for it.

challenge: Is 'boring onboarding' a differentiator? Incumbents and adjacent vendors already sell migration services and tooling.
evidence: Ren sells a Data Migration service (ONB-021) and says it has 'transitioned many existing DAF programs'. Give Interactive markets data migration. akoyaGO claims accounting migrations cut from 15 days to 2-3 days, with 32 go-lives in 2025. Foundant publishes per-source conversion templates. The Salesforce ecosystem sells AI-driven migration accelerators and fixed-price 14-week packages. TIFIN markets a donor-switch workflow. None publishes full history, a reconciliation proof, the length of the user-visible freeze, or exit terms, but that is 'not publicly documented', not proof of absence.
recommended_revision: Base the claimed differentiation on verifiable outcomes competitors do not publish: the gate register, history depth, freeze length and exit terms. Add a migration-tooling row to the competitor matrix. Test buyer value in interviews before treating migration as a moat. The sales-cycle benefit stays a HYPOTHESIS.

challenge: The 'fits inside 20 bps; payback about 1 month' finding comes from the revenue assumption, not from onboarding cost, and it is stated at too high a confidence. Time-to-production bounds also conflict with the evidence in draft 10.
evidence: At 10k accounts: AUA $2.06B, revenue $4.13M, recurring cost about $480k. Even 10 times the onboarding cost would pay back in about 11 months. 59 of the 91 parameters are ASSUMPTION. Draft 20 says 'no public benchmark' for time to production, yet draft 10 documents Hartford (6 months contract to system of record), AEF (about 8.5 months from selection) and Arizona (18 months or more). The model's low end of 16-18 weeks is below every observed case.
recommended_revision: Lower confidence to Low. Report payback at buyer-anchored prices, for example 10 bps and a per-account price. Calibrate ttp_base_weeks to the cases in draft 10, and add incumbent notice and contract-window lead time.

challenge: The T1 'profile runs on the sponsor's premises' step assumes the sponsor holds its data. With hosted incumbents the sponsor must first get an export, which can be paid, banned from automation, or 'as stored' only. Asking for it may also signal the intent to switch.
evidence: NPact export is a paid PS and §2.4 requires direct login. TIFIN bars downloading. Foundant export is CSV 'as stored' through reporting tools.
recommended_revision: Define T1 inputs as standard reports the sponsor can run through direct login. Add an incumbent-specific extract catalogue. Make export rights and costs a T0 output.

challenge: Numeric design parameters disagree across drafts.
evidence: Freeze: 2 business days or less (10) against 3 or less (11, 17). Dry runs: at least 2 (10) against at least 3 rehearsals (11). Blackout: 1 Nov-31 Jan (11) against a hard Dec 15-Jan 5 plus 'prefer Mar-Sep' (17). AEF history: '2 years' (10, 11) against '33 months' (13). Both AEF figures are right: 33 months pulled, 2 years reviewable (ADVB-005).
recommended_revision: Keep one parameter table, owned by draft 17, and have drafts 10, 11 and 20 reference it. State AEF as '33 months imported, 2 years visible'.

challenge: Overclaim. Draft 11 calls AEF 'the only public DAF platform-change evidence' at VERIFIED-FACT, High.
evidence: Draft 10 documents GWCF, Lehigh Valley, Winston-Salem, CF of Acadiana and ImpactAssets platform changes, all DAF-holding sponsors. ADVB-006 confirms GWCF.
recommended_revision: Reword to 'the only national-sponsor case found'.

challenge: Draft 17 cites a 60-day return window to route returns of legacy-originated grant credits. The cited window (R10) applies to unauthorized consumer debits.
evidence: MIG-022's own excerpt says 'unauthorized consumer debit returns (R10) within 60 calendar days'. Grants are credit entries. The Nacha rules were not read directly.
recommended_revision: Restate using the return codes for credit entries and the ODFI agreement. A conservative retention window can stay, but justify it on its own terms.

challenge: Tested and rejected: 'the drafts misreport incumbent contract terms or vendor timelines'.
evidence: Checked against primary pages: Foundant MSA (30-day termination for convenience, pro-rata refund, CSV as stored, billable custom export), NPact (10 business days, 3-year term, 90-day notice), Ren (90-120 days, about $50k), NPT (14-16 weeks), Foundation Source (a few business days), GWCF (7 years), akoyaGO (85%), Fidelity (5 minutes). All match. One nuance: Foundant's 30 days is a 'return or erase' window and the export is due only on written request at termination.
recommended_revision: No change beyond adding the Foundant nuance and its §11.3 one-year employee non-solicit to the table in draft 10.

challenge: Tested and rejected: 'the cross-industry anchors are misquoted'.
evidence: FINRA 11870 (1 and 3 business days, closed exception list), CASS (1,190,676 switches, 99.7% within 7 working days, 160.5m redirections cumulative) and ERISA (30-60 days' notice, more than 3 consecutive business days) all match the primary sources. The weakness is the analogy (ADVB-03), not the citation.
